To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incorporation of a fluoropyridine moiety on the cyclic triimidazole scaffold enhances the molecular properties of the latter, resulting in a high PLQY in solution and preserving the solid-state RT-UP.
the fluoropyridinic group enhances the photoluminescence of cyclic-triimidazoles, preserving at the same time their RTUP properties.

we discovered a new room-temperature dual phosphorescence from 2-fluoropyridine-triimidazole derivative, which is characterized by a very high PLQY in solution, a very long phosphorescence in solid state and a long-lived RTUP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a novel multifunctional phosphorescent molecule that can be used in different matrices to obtain different emission colors.
a new class of organic materials that combine the advantages of the high PLQY in solution and the RTUP in solid state.
the design of a new molecular system able to emit in solid state with a dual phosphorescence, one of which at room temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3-(2-fluoropyridine-4-yl)-triiimidazo[1,2-a:1',2'-c:1'',2''-e][1,3,5]triazines are a class of compounds that exhibit a complex photoluminescence behavior.
the fluoropyridinic group enhances the molecular properties and, as such, the fluorescence, but does not affect the formation of aggregates and the consequent RTUP.

the fluoropyridinic moiety is able to enhance the photoluminescence of the cyclic-tri-imidazole core by promoting the S1 emission in solution and in PMM blends and the T1 emission in frozen solution and PMMA blends, and to induce H-aggregate formation in the solid state, which in turn results in RTUP emission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the introduction of the fluoropyridinic moiety on the cyclic-triidimidazole scaffold, which has a positive effect on the photophysical properties of the compound, does not prevent the formation of H aggregates in the solid state.

the incorporation of a fluorinated pyridinic moiety in the triimidazolic scaffold results in a dual phosphorescence system with the possibility to tune the relative intensity of fluorescence and phosphorescent components by varying the solvent polarity.

, by means of a simple chemical manipulation, it is possible to modulate the photophysical properties of cyclic-triimidazoles in a wide range, thus opening new perspectives for their applications in the field of organic luminescence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the introduction of a fluoropyridine moiety in a cyclic-triimidazo[1′,2’-c][1,2,3]triazine framework results in a compound that is characterized by a high PL QY in solution, but preserves the RTUP property of its precursor.

the introduction of a fluoropyridinyl substituent in cyclic-triimidazoles is a promising way to tune their photophysical properties, thus opening new perspectives towards the design of efficient room temperature persistent organic phosphors.
the combination of a fluorinated and a triimidazole moiety is a promising strategy for the development of multifaceted organic room temperature phosphorescent materials.
